newsitem.title: USA: Israel's Peres hails Hebron agreement.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Peres hails Hebron agreement.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres said on Wednesday that Israel's agreement to withdraw from the West Bank city of Hebron marked the end of the idea that Israel should control all the biblical land of Israel regardless of who lives there.
"The idea of keeping all the land (regardless) of its demographic division is over," Peres told reporters after telephoning Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to congratulate him.
"This is the beginning of the end of a deep ideological rift that ... divided the Israeli people from the first day of its creation," he added.

Peres said that rift pitted those who believed Israel should control all of biblical Israel against those, like the country's first prime minister, David Ben-Gurion, who believed it should control lands with a Jewish majority or those needed by the state for security reasons.
"A great argument is over, I can see a time and point when we can arrive at permanent borders," he added.

Perez, in New York to attend a dinner for Israel's Peace Now movement, said the deal reached by Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat was very similar to the one he reached with Arafat 11 months ago.
"Nobody won anything by postponing it ... Israel has lost a little bit of goodwill unnecessarily, yet I have to say the problems they had (reaching the agreement) are very serious," he added.

Netanyahu and Arafat bowed to intense U.S. political pressure and clinched the long-delayed Hebron accord at an overnight summit. They also agreed Israel would complete three further pullbacks in the West Bank over the next 18 months.

Netanyahu brought the agreement to his cabinet on Wednesday, which seemed likely to approve it, although up to seven of the 18 ministers could oppose it. Arafat was also scheduled to put the still unpublished accord to his cabinet on Wednesday night.
The accord was an ideological wrench for Netanyahu and his Likud party who have vowed never to cede part of the biblical Land of Israel to Palestinians.
